new.title: Collapse all closes every Tech View group and Expand all opens them
preconds: Sign in to the Work Orders build under test as a user whose role has Work Orders view. To check: Settings > Roles & Permissions > open the role > Work Orders (an Owner or Admin role has it).
Use a desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide. Narrower windows show only the List, without the display switcher.
In the top bar, pick the location you will test in (e.g. "Heavy Duty") and stay in it for the whole case.

At least 2 technicians are eligible at this location (e.g. "Esther Howard", "Ralph Edwards"). A staff member is eligible when Clockable is on, the staff record is Active, the role is neither Office nor Time Clock User, and they are enrolled at this location. To add one:
↳ Settings > Staff > add a staff member, enter a first and last name (e.g. "Ralph Edwards") and an email.
↳ Pick a role that is not Office or Time Clock User (e.g. "Technician"), turn Clockable on, keep the record Active, enrol the staff member at this location, then Save.

Create a customer used only by this case so a search shows only its work orders: Customers > New Customer, name (e.g. "ZZ Board Test Co"), add an asset with a unit number and year/make/model (e.g. unit "TRK-118", "2022 Freightliner M2"), then Save.

Create three work orders for that customer: Work Orders > New Work Order > pick the case customer (e.g. "ZZ Board Test Co") and its asset > create it. Write down the number the build gives each one (e.g. "S1-702", "S1-644", "S1-389"; the numbers in this case are examples).
↳ On the first work order's page set Lead Technician to "Esther Howard". On the second set it to "Ralph Edwards". Leave the third with no lead technician so it sits in Unassigned.
If you collapsed any Tech View group before, open Work Orders > Tech View and expand it again, so every group starts open.
steps: Open Work Orders.
Click the All tab.
Type the case customer's name (e.g. "ZZ Board Test Co") in Search.
In the display switcher at the right of the toolbar, click Tech View (in the design its tooltip reads "By Lead Tech").
Hover the button at the left end of the column-heading row, above the group arrows (in the design its tooltip reads "Collapse all").
Click that button.
Hover the same button again.
Refresh the page.
Click the same button.
Collapse Ralph Edwards' group only (arrow on his header).
Click the button at the left end of the column-heading row.
results: Step 5: the tooltip says the button collapses all groups (the design reads "Collapse all"). Write down the words you see; a different label alone is not a fail.

Step 6: every group closes at once, Unassigned included. Unassigned, Esther Howard and Ralph Edwards show only their headers, and their counts do not change (with the example data: Unassigned 1, Esther Howard 1, Ralph Edwards 1). Groups of other technicians with no matching work close too.
Step 7: the tooltip now says the button expands all groups (the design reads "Expand all").
Step 8: after the refresh every group is still closed, Unassigned included.
Step 9: every group opens at once and shows its rows again: S1-702 under Esther Howard, S1-644 under Ralph Edwards, S1-389 under Unassigned. The tooltip goes back to "Collapse all".
Step 11: with one group closed and the others open, the button closes every group. It does not open Ralph Edwards' group.
No work order changes group, the tab and the search text stay the same, and no message appears.
If the build has no such button in Tech View, mark the case Blocked with the comment "no Collapse all button in the build" so it can be raised with the product owner.
new.source: Epic SV-10043; story SV-10045 (Story 2, Tech View — table grouped by lead technician); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S2-R5, S2-R13, S2-R18, read 8 Oct 2026. Design export of 8 Oct 2026 (Branko Cicovic, Claude Design project 787fef1a, Work Orders.dc.html): Tech View column-heading row button with tooltip "Collapse all" / "Expand all" (template line 34; label rule line 1304: "Collapse all" while any group is open, otherwise "Expand all"; toggleAll lines 980-986: closes every group when any is open, otherwise opens every group). Design crawl 8 Oct 2026, Tech View states 0-4, hover and click "Collapse all". The button is a design-only addition (the PRD neither asks for it nor rules it out); that the closed state is kept after a refresh comes from S2-R13. Source-verified 8 October 2026; not yet build-verified.
quotes: Allow each technician group to be collapsed or expanded.
Save group collapse state per user. It is kept after refreshes, logout/login, new tabs, and reopening the page.

Unassigned opens expanded unless the user collapsed it (S2-R13), and its header stays on screen while scrolling so it can be collapsed from anywhere. When it holds more work orders than fit on screen, which on the All tab can be thousands, it loads them in pages as the user scrolls, as List does, never all at once.

new.title: Searching in the Reassign lead technician dialog narrows the technician list
preconds: Sign in to the Work Orders build under test as a user whose role has Work Orders view and Work Orders create and edit. To check: Settings > Roles & Permissions > open the role > Work Orders (an Owner or Admin role has both).
Use a desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide. Narrower windows show only the List, without the display switcher.
In the top bar, pick the location you will test in (e.g. "Heavy Duty") and stay in it for the whole case.

At least 3 technicians are eligible at this location (e.g. "Esther Howard", "Ralph Edwards", "Dana Ortiz"). A staff member is eligible when Clockable is on, the staff record is Active, the role is neither Office nor Time Clock User, and they are enrolled at this location. To add one:
↳ Settings > Staff > add a staff member, enter a first and last name (e.g. "Dana Ortiz") and an email.
↳ Pick a role that is not Office or Time Clock User (e.g. "Technician"), turn Clockable on, keep the record Active, enrol the staff member at this location, then Save.
One staff member who must NOT be offered: an Office-role user (e.g. "Owen Office"). Create them the same way under Settings > Staff, but pick the Office role.

Create a customer used only by this case so a search shows only its work orders: Customers > New Customer, name (e.g. "ZZ Board Test Co"), add an asset with a unit number and year/make/model (e.g. unit "TRK-118", "2022 Freightliner M2"), then Save.
Create the work order: Work Orders > New Work Order > pick the case customer (e.g. "ZZ Board Test Co") and its asset > create it, and write down its number (e.g. "S1-702").
On the work order page set Lead Technician to "Esther Howard".
On the Lines tab click New Line, enter a name (e.g. "Brake inspection") and labor hours (e.g. 2.0), and save the line.
Click the line's Approve (check) button so the work order status reads Approved.
steps: Open Work Orders, click the All tab and pick Board View in the display switcher (right side of the toolbar; in the design its button tooltip reads "Board").
Type the case customer's name (e.g. "ZZ Board Test Co") in Search.
Hover the work order's card (e.g. "S1-702") in Esther Howard's column and click its More actions (…) button.
Choose Reassign lead technician.
Read the top of the dialog and the list of choices.
Click the dialog's search box (in the design it reads "Search technicians") and type Ral
Clear the search box and type ral (all lower case).
Clear the search box and type Owen
Clear the search box and type zzqx
Clear the search box.
Click Cancel.
Open the same card's More actions menu again and choose Reassign lead technician.
Read the search box.
Click Cancel.
Pick Tech View in the display switcher and repeat steps 3 to 14 using the row's More actions (…) button.
results: Step 5: the dialog names the work order it is changing, by number and customer (in the design: "S1-702 · ZZ Board Test Co"), and marks Esther Howard as the current lead (the design highlights her with a check mark). Write down what you see; a different layout alone is not a fail.
Step 5: the list offers Unassigned and the eligible technicians of this location, e.g. Esther Howard, Ralph Edwards and Dana Ortiz.
Step 6: only technicians whose name contains "Ral" stay in the list: Ralph Edwards. Esther Howard and Dana Ortiz disappear from it.
Step 7: lower-case "ral" gives the same list, Ralph Edwards only. Upper or lower case does not matter.
Step 8: no technician is listed for "Owen". Owen Office has the Office role and is never offered, not even by searching.
Steps 8 and 9: when nothing matches, the dialog says so and repeats what you typed (in the design: No technicians match “zzqx”). Write down the words you see; a different wording alone is not a fail.
Step 10: clearing the search box brings back the whole list from step 5.
Step 11: nothing changes. The card stays in Esther Howard's column and no message appears.
Step 13: the search box is empty when the dialog opens again.
Step 15: Tech View behaves the same way, and the row stays in Esther Howard's group.
new.source: Epic SV-10043; story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S4-R12, S4-R14 and section 8 "Design updates required from Branko" (Reassign dialog content and search), read 8 Oct 2026. Eligibility from PRD section 5 Terminology (Technician). Design export of 8 Oct 2026 (Branko Cicovic, Claude Design project 787fef1a, Work Orders.dc.html): Reassign dialog subtitle "work order number · customer" (assignSub, line 1363), search box "Search technicians" (line 357) keeping the technicians whose name contains the typed text in any letter case (lines 1180-1181), current lead highlighted with a check mark, no-match text "No technicians match “the typed text”" (line 1366), search emptied each time the dialog opens (openAssign, line 900). Design crawl 8 Oct 2026: Board View state 225 and Tech View state 193 ("S1-702 · Fibridge Commercial"), Board View states 227-228 ("No technicians match “Fib”", "No technicians match “zzqx-no-match”"). Design-only details (subtitle, search behaviour, no-match text, current-lead mark) are cited to the design; the PRD does not fix their wording. The list content (eligible technicians and Unassigned) follows S4-R12. Source-verified 8 October 2026; not yet build-verified.
quotes: The dialog offers eligible active technicians in the current location and Unassigned.
Canceling the dialog leaves the lead unchanged.
Reassign dialog content, search, grouping, avatars, and exact “N open” count.

Use a desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide. Narrower windows show only the List, without the display switcher.
In the top bar, pick the location you will test in (e.g. "Heavy Duty") and stay in it for the whole case.

At least 1 technicians are eligible at this location (e.g. "Esther Howard"). A staff member is eligible when Clockable is on, the staff record is Active, the role is neither Office nor Time Clock User, and they are enrolled at this location. To add one:
↳ Settings > Staff > add a staff member, enter a first and last name (e.g. "Esther Howard") and an email.
↳ Pick a role that is not Office or Time Clock User (e.g. "Technician"), turn Clockable on, keep the record Active, enrol the staff member at this location, then Save.

Create a customer used only by this case so a search shows only its work orders: Customers > New Customer, name (e.g. "ZZ Board Test Co"), add an asset with a unit number and year/make/model (e.g. unit "TRK-118", "2022 Freightliner M2"), then Save.
Create the work order: Work Orders > New Work Order > pick the case customer (e.g. "ZZ Board Test Co") and its asset > create it, and write down its number (e.g. "S1-702").
On the work order page set Lead Technician to "Esther Howard".
steps: Open Work Orders.
Click the All tab.
Type the case customer's name (e.g. "ZZ Board Test Co") in Search.
In the display switcher at the right of the toolbar, click Tech View (in the design its tooltip reads "By Lead Tech").
Write down every column heading in Esther Howard's group.
Click the Columns button in the toolbar (in the design its tooltip reads "Columns").
Write down the count beside the menu heading (e.g. "10 of 10 shown") and every column listed with its tick.
Click the menu's search box (in the design it reads "Find a column") and type ass
Clear the box and type ASS (all capitals).
Clear the box and type zzqx
Clear the box.
Close the Columns menu by clicking outside it.
In the display switcher, click Board View (in the design its tooltip reads "Board").
Click Fields to display in the toolbar (the same place as Columns in Tech View).
Type zzqx in its search box, then clear the box.
results: Step 8: only the columns whose name contains "ass" stay listed (e.g. "Asset" and "Assigned Techs"). The other columns disappear from the menu but keep their ticks.
Step 9: capitals give the same list. Upper or lower case does not matter.
Step 10: no column is listed and the menu says nothing matches (in the design: "No columns match"). Write down the words you see; a different wording alone is not a fail.
Steps 8 to 10: typing never ticks or unticks anything. The count from step 7 and the column headings from step 5 stay exactly the same.
Step 11: clearing the box brings back every column from step 7, each with the same tick.

Steps 14 and 15: Fields to display works the same way as the Columns menu: its search box narrows the field list by name, a search that finds nothing says so, and clearing it brings every field back with the same ticks. If Board View has no Fields to display button, mark the case Failed and write "no Fields to display picker" in the comment (the design has none; this is a known difference).
new.source: Epic SV-10043; story SV-10048 (Story 5, Fields to display (Board View) and columns (Tech View)); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S2-R4, S5-R2, read 8 Oct 2026. Design export of 8 Oct 2026 (Branko Cicovic, Claude Design project 787fef1a, Work Orders.dc.html) renders the Columns menu through the design system bundle _ds/shopview-design-system-fac6efcf…/_ds_bundle.js: search box "Find a column" (line 552), the menu keeps the columns whose name contains the typed text in any letter case (line 556), no-match text "No columns match" (line 580); ticks are kept separately from the search. Design crawl 8 Oct 2026: Tech View state 123 (Columns > Find a column, typed "Fib" and "zzqx-no-match": "10 of 10 shown | No columns match"). The search box and its wording are design-only details cited to the design; that Board View's Fields to display behaves the same way comes from S5-R2. Board View's missing Fields to display picker in the design is already recorded as a design-vs-spec difference. Source-verified 8 October 2026; not yet build-verified.

Board View offers a separate Fields to display picker in the same toolbar position and with the same interaction as the column chooser.
